source.title: Scaling Laws in the Tiny Regime: How Small Models Change Their Mistakes
source.authors: Mohammed Alnemari; Rizwan Qureshi; N. Bagherzadeh

record.tranche_reason: The study measures image-model scaling and reports architecture-dependent exponents, curvature, and saturation, refining the scope of power-law scaling claims.
record.gate_note: The study's own experiments are on CIFAR-100 image classifiers, not language models. The related-work statements about Kaplan, Hoffmann, and other studies are citations, not results from this study. Its principal fit is to test error rate, not held-out cross-entropy; the reported cross-entropy fits are for training loss.
record.test_reason: The study trains 90 width-scaled CIFAR-100 image classifiers (22K–19.8M parameters, two families) and fits power laws to test error. This is a new setting (small image models, error rate) with direct results on whether the power-law form holds there (V5). It also reports architecture-dependent exponents, metric-dependent exponents and bending local slopes (V7). It does not touch language-model loss, extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation or downstream prediction.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that approximate power laws in error rate extend to sub-20M CIFAR-100 models, with architecture-dependent exponents (0.156, 0.106). Scaling is not uniform: local exponents decay and MobileNetV2 saturates. Exponent comparison with LLM cross-entropy is only approximate. Their main emphasis, which the paraphrase omits, is that smaller models change which inputs they misclassify (Jaccard 0.35), triage classes, and are best calibrated by ECE. They argue aggregate accuracy is insufficient and validation must happen at deployment size.
record.recipe_differences: Trains width-scaled image classifiers from scratch on CIFAR-100 and fits test error rate, with additional training-loss fits; it does not reproduce language-model held-out cross-entropy or compute-optimal allocation experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture family changes the fitted exponent and fit quality; local exponents vary with scale, including oscillation at small MobileNetV2 widths and saturation at large widths. The study also notes that error rate and cross-entropy produce very different fitted exponents.

fits_no_version.finding: At matched ~2.5M parameters, ScaleCNN reaches 73.8% accuracy vs MobileNetV2's 67.0%, so the architecture family changes performance substantially in small image models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In small image classifiers, architecture family (plain conv vs inverted-residual) changes accuracy at fixed parameter count by several points, unlike the shape-insensitivity reported for language models.

fits_no_version.finding: Error sets change with scale (Jaccard 0.35 between smallest and largest), class inequality falls (Gini 0.26 → 0.09), and ECE follows an inverted U.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scaling changes which errors a model makes and how calibrated it is, not just the aggregate error.

record.code_released: not stated; the text says training code, analysis scripts, and result files will be released on GitHub upon publication, but gives no URL.
record.peer_reviewed: Machine Learning and Knowledge Extraction (venue stated in the record)
record.problems: Single dataset and two architecture families; width is the only scaling axis, so parameter count, FLOPs, and activation memory are correlated. The principal fits are to test error rate rather than held-out cross-entropy; training cross-entropy is not test loss. There are only 8 and 10 model sizes, and the authors say the fits cannot distinguish a power law from other smooth forms. Upper-end results include substantial overparameterization and saturation.

untested.parts: All of it: no language models and no held-out pretraining cross-entropy.
All of it: no fit on small runs is used to predict larger runs.
All of it: no fixed-compute sweep or allocation of parameters vs tokens.
Depth is held fixed within each family. It does not vary depth or width at fixed parameter count on held-out loss.
All of it: no downstream-task prediction from scale or loss.

Scaling in data or compute (only width/parameters vary). Held-out cross-entropy (only error rate and training loss). Other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer. Datasets other than CIFAR-100. The text says the R2 values cannot discriminate a power law from other smooth forms.
Dependence of the compute-optimal split; parameter-counting conventions; training schedule or data choices; comparison of fitting methods (AIC/BIC not done).

missing.what: Significance test of the exponent difference between architectures (t=50.9, p<1e-6 on per-seed exponents), plus ScaleCNN per-seed R2 range 0.961–0.970.
Authors' statement that 8–10 sizes cannot discriminate a power law from log-linear or BNSL forms, and that Fig. 1b residuals show systematic curvature.
400-epoch spot check: accuracy changed <0.3% for three ScaleCNN configurations, so the 200-epoch results are near asymptotic.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed from T5 to T3: this is a new setting with direct results, not mainly an argument against a version. The reader's V7 limits_scope label was dropped, because the metric-mismatch caveat strengthens V7 rather than limiting it. The MobileNetV2 saturation happens at a 396:1 parameter-to-sample ratio, i.e. data-bottlenecked, so it is labelled limits_scope rather than challenges. The record's peer_reviewed field names a journal venue not stated in the text; the text is an arXiv v1 preprint with no venue given.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining cross-entropy loss in language models, and loss scaling across parameters, tokens, and compute when the other factors are not bottlenecks.
No experiment fits on small runs and evaluates predictions on runs orders of magnitude larger.
No fixed-compute-budget sweep or compute-optimal allocation of parameters and tokens.
The study does not compare held-out loss across depth, width, or architecture details at fixed parameter count; depth is held fixed within each family.

Tests image classification on one dataset, with width scaling and error rate (plus training loss), not other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer; it does not test held-out pretraining loss.
No downstream-task performance prediction from scale or pretraining loss.

Tests architecture-dependent fitted exponents, nonuniform local scaling, and metric differences. It does not test compute-optimal split dependence or directly compare alternative fitting procedures such as AIC/BIC.

rows.subject: ScaleCNN
rows.operation_detail: Fit a power law to CIFAR-100 top-1 test error rate across model sizes; aggregate fit across five seeds.
rows.measure: Top-1 test error rate versus parameter count; fitted exponent and R2
rows.uncertainty: ±0.002 standard deviation across five seeds; 95% CI [0.154, 0.158]
rows.note: Aggregate fit reported for the ScaleCNN size sweep. This is an image-classification error-rate fit, not held-out cross-entropy.

source_check.locator_found: Sections 4.2–4.5; Section 5.1, Equation 8 and following paragraph.

rows.subject: MobileNetV2
rows.operation_detail: Fit a power law to CIFAR-100 top-1 test error rate across model sizes; aggregate fit across five seeds.
rows.measure: Top-1 test error rate versus parameter count; fitted exponent and R2
rows.uncertainty: ±0.001 standard deviation across five seeds; 95% CI [0.105, 0.107]
rows.note: Aggregate fit reported for the MobileNetV2 size sweep. The fit is weaker than ScaleCNN's, and the text relates this to oscillatory local exponents and saturation. The measure is test error rate, not held-out cross-entropy.
rows.check: State fine. R2 = 0.914 (per-seed 0.860–0.928) is weaker than ScaleCNN's 0.965 but passes the authors' own R2 ≥ 0.9 criterion. The authors attribute the weaker fit to oscillation and saturation.

source_check.correct: State: partial for V5; observed for V7. The weaker aggregate fit, architecture-dependent exponent and nonuniform local slopes exhibit V7.
source_check.locator_found: Section 5.1, Equation 9 and following paragraphs; Sections 5.2–5.3.
source_check.problem: The shared partial state fits V5 but understates the observed fit dependence and curvature relevant to V7.

rows.subject: ScaleCNN
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch; final training loss at epoch 200
rows.operation_detail: Fit a power law to final training cross-entropy loss across model sizes; aggregate fit across five seeds.
rows.measure: Final training cross-entropy versus parameter count; fitted exponent
rows.note: The authors explicitly caution that this is training loss, not test loss; they state the largest models are heavily overfit.
rows.check: This is training cross-entropy of heavily overfit models, not held-out loss, and no R2 is given. It cannot show whether a power law holds (V5). It bears on V7 only: the exponent is 5× the error-rate exponent, so the metric choice changes the fitted law.

source_check.locator_found: Section 5.1, paragraph reporting final training cross-entropy fits.

rows.subject: MobileNetV2
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch; final training loss at epoch 200
rows.operation_detail: Fit a power law to final training cross-entropy loss across model sizes; aggregate fit across five seeds.
rows.measure: Final training cross-entropy versus parameter count; fitted exponent
rows.note: The authors explicitly caution that this is training loss, not test loss.
rows.check: Training loss, not held-out, with no R2, so it does not bear on V5. For V7: 0.30 vs 0.106 for error rate (3×) shows the exponent depends on the metric.

source_check.locator_found: Section 5.1, paragraph reporting final training cross-entropy fits.

rows.subject: ScaleCNN
rows.operation_detail: Calculate finite-difference local scaling exponents between adjacent model sizes.
rows.value: Smooth monotonic decay from 0.23 below 100K parameters to 0.10 near 5M parameters
rows.note: The study describes this as smoothly bending scaling rather than a single uniform exponent.
rows.check: Partial for V5: the single-exponent form holds only approximately, since the local slope falls from 0.23 to 0.10. Observed for V7: the curve bends away from a single power law, with systematic curvature in the Fig. 1b residuals.

source_check.correct: State: partial for V5; observed for V7. ScaleCNN local exponents decline smoothly from 0.23 below 100K parameters to 0.10 near 5M.
source_check.locator_found: Section 5.2, Figure 2 caption and following ScaleCNN paragraph.
source_check.problem: The partial state fits V5, but the reported curvature directly exhibits V7.

rows.subject: MobileNetV2
rows.operation_detail: Calculate finite-difference local exponents between the stated adjacent width multipliers.
rows.note: Part of the reported oscillation in local exponents at small widths.
rows.check: A single local slope can't be judged against V5 on its own. Together, r6–r8 show the oscillation 0.44 → 0.08 → 0.23, which is non-uniform scaling (V7). The per-row states observed/partial on individual slopes are not meaningful.

rows.subject: MobileNetV2
rows.operation_detail: Calculate finite-difference local exponent between adjacent width multipliers.
rows.note: Part of the reported oscillation in local exponents at small widths.
rows.check: Part of the r6–r8 oscillation. The state applies to the group (non-uniform local exponent), not to this single value.

rows.subject: MobileNetV2
rows.operation_detail: Calculate finite-difference local exponent between adjacent width multipliers.
rows.note: Part of the reported oscillation in local exponents at small widths.
rows.check: Part of the r6–r8 oscillation; see r6.

rows.subject: MobileNetV2
rows.operation_detail: Calculate local exponents at the upper end of the size sweep.
rows.note: Part of the reported decline in local exponent with increasing size.
rows.check: αlocal = 0.094 at m = 1.0→1.5 is close to the aggregate 0.106, so scaling still holds here.

rows.subject: MobileNetV2
rows.operation_detail: Calculate local exponents at the upper end of the size sweep.
rows.note: The table describes this range as diminishing returns.
rows.check: αlocal = 0.040 is well under half the aggregate exponent; the text calls this diminishing returns.

source_check.correct: State: partial for V5; observed for V7. The local exponent is 0.040 at m = 1.5 → 2.0, described as diminishing returns.
source_check.problem: The partial state fits V5, while the declining exponent exhibits V7.

rows.subject: MobileNetV2
rows.operation_detail: Compare the final adjacent width-multiplier configurations and report the local exponent and accuracy gain.
rows.measure: Local exponent αlocal and top-1 accuracy gain
rows.note: The authors describe this as effective architectural saturation; they report that it is not observed in ScaleCNN up to its smaller maximum size.
rows.check: For V5 the improvement is effectively zero (αlocal = 0.006, +0.14%); the authors call it saturation. This occurs at a 396:1 parameter-to-sample ratio, i.e. where data is the bottleneck. Observed for V7 as bending.

source_check.correct: State: absent for V5; observed for V7. Accuracy rises from 70.01% to 70.15%; the reported gain is +0.14%, with local exponent 0.006 and effective saturation.
source_check.locator_found: Table 2, MobileNetV2 m = 2.00 and 3.00; Section 5.3, transition table and following paragraph.
source_check.problem: The absent state fits the negligible scaling improvement under V5, but saturation directly exhibits V7.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-100 width scaling, aggregate fits for ScaleCNN (22K–4.7M) and MobileNetV2 (214K–19.8M)
relationships.reason: Test error follows approximate power laws: r1 α=0.156, R2=0.965; r2 α=0.106, R2=0.914, both stable over 5 seeds.
relationships.display_finding: Test error fitted approximate power laws with α=0.156 and R²=0.965 for ScaleCNN and α=0.106 and R²=0.914 for MobileNetV2, stable across five seeds.

relationships.condition: Local slopes across the range, and MobileNetV2 above m=1.5 where data (50K images) becomes the bottleneck
relationships.reason: The local exponent decays from 0.23 to 0.10 (r5). MobileNetV2 falls to 0.040 and then 0.006 (r10, r11). The authors also say R2 cannot distinguish a power law from other smooth forms (text).
relationships.display_finding: The local exponent decreased from 0.23 to 0.10, while MobileNetV2 exponents fell to 0.040 and then 0.006; R² could not distinguish power laws from other smooth forms.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Local slopes across the range, and MobileNetV2 above m=1.5 where data (50K images) becomes the bottleneck
source_check.reason: r5 shows systematic slope decay; r10 and r11 show diminishing returns followed by effective saturation. These mixed local results qualify the aggregate power-law description. The text identifies severe overparameterization at the endpoint, without isolating its cause experimentally.

relationships.display_finding: Architecture exponents differed with t=50.9, changing the metric produced 3–5× steeper slopes, and local slopes bent and oscillated.
